title: Recent advances in the assembly of high-nuclearity lanthanide clusters
claim: Multiple copies of the same oxoanion, not only mixed anion types, can stitch many small hydroxo motifs into giant cages or tubes, with the anions both templating faces or wheels and supporting the skeleton.
explanation: Er60 is built from 24 cubanes that share corners into square {Er12} and hexagonal {Er18} units; eight μ6-carbonates, generated from L-threonine decomposition, sit in the hexagons and join two {Er36} sections. Dy72 uses many nitrates on outer {Dy24} wheels of a saddle-like tube of triangles, rhombi and square pyramids. Ln104 (Nd/Gd) uses six perchlorates: hydrogen bonding between μ3-OH and perchlorate oxygen templates cross-shaped {Ln16} wheels of square pyramids, which with eight {Ln(μ3-OH)6} units give the four-shell Ln8@Ln48@Ln24@Ln24 cage.
scope: Highest-nuclearity lanthanide-exclusive clusters surveyed (Er60, Dy72, Ln104).
conditions: Er60: controlled hydrolysis of Er(ClO4)3 with L-threonine. Ln104: hydrolysis of Ln(ClO4)3 with Co(CH3COO)2·4H2O and N-acetyl-D-glucosamine. Dy72: mda/mdaH ligands with nitrate.
caveats: Ln104 is described as the highest-nuclearity lanthanide-exclusive clusters reported at the time of the review; that ranking is time-bound.
